q: किस विचारक ने अपनी प्रसिद्ध 1748 की कृति 'द स्पिरिट ऑफ द लॉज़' में 'शक्ति पृथक्करण' (Separation of Powers) के शास्त्रीय सिद्धांत का प्रतिपादन किया?
e:
French political philosopher Baron de Montesquieu formulated the modern doctrine of Separation of Powers among Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary in 'The Spirit of the Laws' (1748) to safeguard individual liberty (मॉन्टेस्क्यू ने शक्ति पृथक्करण का सिद्धांत प्रतिपादित किया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. The US Constitution (1787) embodies the strictest application of Separation of Powers along with 'Checks and Balances'.
2. In India, Article 50 (DPSP) directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services.
3. Walter Bagehot described the Cabinet as a 'buckle' that joins the legislative and executive branches in a parliamentary system.
qe: Which thinker propounded the classical theory of 'Separation of Powers' in his celebrated 1748 treatise 'The Spirit of the Laws' (De l'esprit des lois)?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी संसदीय शासन प्रणाली की सर्वाधिक अनिवार्य विशेषता है?
o: Fixed tenure of the Chief Executive
Strict separation between Legislature and Executive
Collective responsibility of the Executive to the Legislature
Direct popular election of the Head of State
e:
Collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the lower house of the Legislature (Article 75(3) in India) is the bedrock principle of Parliamentary government (संसदीय शासन प्रणाली में कार्यपालिका की विधायिका के प्रति सामूहिक उत्तरदायित्व सबसे प्रमुख विशेषता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Parliamentary government is also called 'Cabinet Government', 'Responsible Government', or the 'Westminster Model'.
2. It features a dual executive: Nominal Head of State (President/Monarch) and Real Head of Government (Prime Minister).
3. Presidential system (e.g., USA) features a single executive, fixed tenure (4 years), and non-responsibility of the President to Congress.
qe: Which of the following is the most essential defining feature of a Parliamentary form of government?
oe: Fixed tenure of the Chief Executive
Strict separation between Legislature and Executive
Collective responsibility of the Executive to the Legislature
Direct popular election of the Head of State

q: अध्यक्षात्मक (राष्ट्रपति) शासन प्रणाली के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
o: The President is both Head of State and Head of Government.
Cabinet members are chosen by the President and are responsible to him.
The President can dissolve the lower house of the Legislature at any time.
The President enjoys a fixed tenure and can be removed only through impeachment.
e:
In a Presidential system (like the USA), the President CANNOT dissolve the Legislature (Congress), nor can Congress remove the President by a no-confidence motion (अध्यक्षात्मक प्रणाली में राष्ट्रपति विधायिका को भंग नहीं कर सकता)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Because the President cannot dissolve the Legislature, legislative deadlocks can occur when the President's party lacks a majority in Congress.
2. In the US Presidential system, ministers (Secretaries) are NOT members of Congress.
3. France and Sri Lanka follow a Semi-Presidential system combining elements of both models.
qe: Which of the following statements about a Presidential form of government is NOT correct?
oe: The President is both Head of State and Head of Government.
Cabinet members are chosen by the President and are responsible to him.
The President can dissolve the lower house of the Legislature at any time.
The President enjoys a fixed tenure and can be removed only through impeachment.

q: किस शासन प्रणाली में सभी शासकीय शक्तियाँ संवैधानिक रूप से एक ही केंद्रीय सत्ता में निहित होती हैं और क्षेत्रीय इकाइयाँ अपनी शक्तियाँ केवल केंद्र से प्राप्त करती हैं?
e:
In a Unitary government (e.g., UK, France, Japan, China), sovereignty and constitutional authority are vested in a single national government (एकात्मक शासन में समस्त शक्तियाँ केंद्र सरकार में निहित होती हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. A Federal system (e.g., USA, Canada, Australia, Switzerland) divides powers constitutionally between the Centre and States via a written, rigid constitution and an independent judiciary.
2. Dicey noted that federalism requires 'a desire for union, not unity'.
3. Unitary states offer uniform laws and administrative efficiency, whereas federations accommodate regional diversity.
qe: In which form of government are all governmental powers constitutionally concentrated in a single central authority, with regional units deriving their powers solely from the centre?

q: भारतीय संघीय व्यवस्था को किस प्रसिद्ध संविधानविद् ने 'अर्ध-संघात्मक' (Quasi-Federal) कहा है?
e:
Prof. K. C. Wheare described India as a 'Quasi-Federal' state (a unitary state with subsidiary federal features rather than a federal state with subsidiary unitary features) (के. सी. व्हीयर ने भारत को अर्ध-संघात्मक कहा)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Granville Austin called Indian federalism 'Cooperative Federalism' (सहकारी संघवाद).
2. Morris-Jones termed it 'Bargaining Federalism' (सौदेबाजी का संघवाद).
3. Ivor Jennings called it a 'Federation with a strong centralizing tendency'.
qe: Who famously described the Indian federal system as 'Quasi-Federal' (अर्ध-संघात्मक)?

q:
संघवाद के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित दो कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: दोहरी नागरिकता विश्व के प्रत्येक संघीय संविधान की एक अनिवार्य सार्वभौमिक विशेषता है।
कथन II: केंद्र-राज्य विवादों का निर्णय करने की शक्ति वाली स्वतंत्र न्यायपालिका संघीय व्यवस्था की एक अनिवार्य विशेषता है।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II
e:
Statement I is incorrect because federations like India and Canada have single citizenship, whereas USA and Switzerland have dual citizenship. Statement II is correct (स्वतंत्र न्यायपालिका संघवाद की अनिवार्य विशेषता है, जबकि दोहरी नागरिकता अनिवार्य नहीं है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. India's federal model is closer to the Canadian model ('Union of States', residuary powers with the Centre, Governor appointed by the Centre).
2. In S. R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994), the Supreme Court declared 'Federalism' part of the Basic Structure of the Indian Constitution.
3. Under Article 131, the Supreme Court exercises Original Jurisdiction in federal disputes between Centre and States.
qe:
Consider the following two statements regarding Federalism:
Statement I: Dual citizenship is a mandatory universal feature of every federal constitution in the world.
Statement II: An independent judiciary with power to adjudicate Centre–State disputes is an essential feature of a federal system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
oe: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II

q: सरकार का कौन-सा अंग मुख्य रूप से कानूनों की व्याख्या करने, नागरिकों के अधिकारों की रक्षा करने और न्यायिक पुनरावलोकन की शक्ति का प्रयोग करने के लिए उत्तरदायी है?
e:
The Judiciary interprets the Constitution and laws, resolves disputes, safeguards Fundamental Rights, and exercises judicial review (न्यायपालिका कानूनों की व्याख्या और अधिकारों की रक्षा करती है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Legislature makes laws; Executive implements/enforces laws; Judiciary adjudicates and interprets laws.
2. Judicial Review originated in the landmark US Supreme Court case Marbury v. Madison (1803, Chief Justice John Marshall).
3. In India, Judicial Review is anchored in Articles 13, 32, 136, 142, and 226.
qe: Which organ of government is primarily responsible for interpreting laws, protecting citizens' rights, and exercising the power of judicial review?

q: कौन-सा देश 'बहुल कार्यपालिका' (Plural Executive) का सर्वोत्तम उदाहरण है, जहाँ कार्यपालिका की शक्ति 7 सदस्यीय संघीय परिषद में निहित होती है?
e:
Switzerland features a 7-member Collegial/Plural Executive (Federal Council) elected by the Federal Assembly for 4 years, where the Presidency rotates annually among members (स्विट्जरलैंड बहुल कार्यपालिका का आदर्श उदाहरण है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Switzerland is also the foremost modern home of Direct Democracy tools: Referendum (जनमत संग्रह), Initiative (आरम्भक), and Recall (प्रत्याह्वान).
2. USA has a Single Presidential Executive; UK and India have Parliamentary Cabinet Executives.
3. Germany follows a Chancellor-led Parliamentary Federal system with a 'Constructive Vote of No-Confidence'.
qe: Which country is the classic example of a 'Plural Executive' (बहुल कार्यपालिका), where executive authority is vested in a 7-member Federal Council?

q: अमेरिका की 'अवरोध एवं संतुलन' (Checks and Balances) प्रणाली में राष्ट्रपति द्वारा हस्ताक्षरित संधियों का अनुसमर्थन और प्रमुख संघीय न्यायिक नियुक्तियों की पुष्टि करने की संवैधानिक शक्ति किसके पास है?
e:
The US Senate (Upper House, 100 members — 2 per state) confirms Presidential appointments (Cabinet, Supreme Court judges, ambassadors) by simple majority and ratifies treaties by a two-thirds majority (अमेरिकी सीनेट को संधियों के अनुसमर्थन व नियुक्तियों की पुष्टि का अधिकार है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. The US Senate is considered the most powerful second chamber (upper house) in the world.
2. Conversely, the UK House of Lords is regarded as one of the weakest upper chambers (after the Parliament Acts of 1911 and 1949).
3. The US President checks Congress via Veto power (including Pocket Veto), while Congress can override a regular veto by a 2/3rd majority in both Houses.
qe: In the US system of 'Checks and Balances', which body has the constitutional power to ratify treaties signed by the President and confirm key federal judicial appointments?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी भारतीय संविधान की एक 'एकात्मक' (गैर-संघीय) विशेषता है?
o: Division of powers in the Seventh Schedule
e:
Single integrated judiciary, All-India Services (IAS, IPS, IFoS under Art. 312), single citizenship, appointment of Governors by the Centre, and Emergency provisions (Arts. 352, 356, 360) are Unitary features of the Indian Constitution (एकीकृत न्यायपालिका और अखिल भारतीय सेवाएँ एकात्मक विशेषताएँ हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Federal features of India: Dual polity, written Constitution, division of powers (7th Schedule), supremacy of Constitution, rigid amendment for federal clauses, independent judiciary, and bicameralism.
2. During a National Emergency (Art. 352), the Indian federal structure converts into a unitary one without a formal constitutional amendment.
3. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar stated that India's Constitution is 'both unitary as well as federal according to the requirements of time and circumstances'.
qe: Which of the following is a UNITARY (non-federal) feature of the Constitution of India?
oe: Division of powers in the Seventh Schedule

q: 'संसदीय संप्रभुता' की अवधारणा — जहाँ संसद कोई भी कानून बना या समाप्त कर सकती है और कोई न्यायालय उसे अवैध घोषित नहीं कर सकता — किस देश की विशिष्ट विशेषता है?
e:
Britain follows Parliamentary Sovereignty (A. V. Dicey), whereas the USA follows Judicial Supremacy; India strikes a synthesis between British Parliamentary Sovereignty and American Judicial Supremacy (संसदीय संप्रभुता ब्रिटेन की विशिष्ट विशेषता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. De Lolme famously remarked that the British Parliament 'can do everything except make a man a woman and a woman a man'.
2. Because Britain has an unwritten/uncodified flexible constitution, ordinary and constitutional laws are amended by the same simple majority.
3. In India, Parliament is NOT sovereign because it is bound by the written Constitution, Fundamental Rights, federal division of powers, and Judicial Review.
qe: The concept of 'Parliamentary Sovereignty' (संसदीय संप्रभुता) — where Parliament can make or unmake any law and no court can invalidate it — is a distinctive feature of which country?

q: किसने शासकों की संख्या और जनहित बनाम स्वहित के आधार पर शासन प्रणालियों को छह रूपों (राजतंत्र/निरंकुश तंत्र, कुलीनतंत्र/अल्पतंत्र, पॉलिटी/लोकतंत्र) में वर्गीकृत किया?
e:
Aristotle ('Politics') presented the classic six-fold classification of constitutions: Normal (public good) — Monarchy, Aristocracy, Polity; Perverted (self-interest) — Tyranny, Oligarchy, Democracy (अरस्तू ने 'पॉलिटिक्स' में शासन का छह-भागों वाला वर्गीकरण किया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Aristotle regarded 'Polity' (constitutional rule by the middle class) as the best practicable form of government.
2. Aristotle is universally revered as the 'Father of Political Science' and 'Father of Comparative Politics'.
3. He studied 158 Greek city-state constitutions before writing 'Politics'.
qe: Who classified governments into six forms — Monarchy/Tyranny, Aristocracy/Oligarchy, and Polity/Democracy — based on the number of rulers and whether they rule in the public interest or self-interest?

q: संसदीय लोकतंत्र में उन स्थायी, राजनीतिक रूप से तटस्थ सिविल सेवकों के समूह को क्या कहा जाता है जो नीति क्रियान्वयन में मंत्रियों की सहायता करते हैं?
e:
Civil servants selected on merit form the Permanent Executive (Bureaucracy), while elected ministers form the Political Executive (स्थायी कार्यपालिका या नौकरशाही राजनीतिक रूप से तटस्थ होती है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Max Weber gave the classic 'Ideal Type' theory of Bureaucracy (hierarchy, written rules, merit, impersonality).
2. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is known as the 'Father of All-India Services' and called civil services the 'Steel Frame of India'.
3. Articles 308–323 (Part XIV) of the Indian Constitution govern Services under the Union and States.
qe: In a Parliamentary democracy, what is the term used for the permanent, politically neutral body of career civil servants who assist ministers in policy execution?

q: आधुनिक लोकतंत्रों में 'प्रत्यायोजित विधान' (Delegated Legislation) की अवधारणा को निम्नलिखित में से कौन सबसे उपयुक्त रूप से वर्णित करता है?
o: Judiciary making laws during parliamentary recess
Citizens directly proposing bills through initiative
State legislatures delegating taxing powers to Panchayats
Executive making detailed rules and regulations under authority granted by the Legislature
e:
Delegated (Subordinate) Legislation occurs when Parliament passes a broad framework statute and delegates rule-making authority for technical details to the Executive (विधायिका द्वारा प्रदत्त अधिकार के तहत कार्यपालिका द्वारा नियम-विनियम बनाना प्रत्यायोजित विधान कहलाता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Delegated legislation saves parliamentary time and handles complex technical matters, though Lord Hewart criticized its excess as 'The New Despotism'.
2. Parliamentary control over delegated legislation is exercised through the Committee on Subordinate Legislation.
3. Judicial control ensures delegated rules do not go 'ultra vires' (beyond the authority of) the parent Act.
qe: Which of the following best describes the phenomenon of 'Delegated Legislation' (प्रत्यायोजित विधान) in modern democracies?
oe: Judiciary making laws during parliamentary recess
Citizens directly proposing bills through initiative
State legislatures delegating taxing powers to Panchayats
Executive making detailed rules and regulations under authority granted by the Legislature

q:
द्विसदनीय विधायिका के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: संघीय व्यवस्था में उच्च सदन सामान्यतः घटक राज्यों या संघीय इकाइयों का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है।
कथन II: भारत में वर्तमान में सभी 28 राज्यों में विधानसभा और विधान परिषद दोनों के साथ द्विसदनीय विधायिका है।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II
e:
Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because only 6 Indian states currently have bicameral legislatures: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana (वर्तमान में भारत के केवल 6 राज्यों में द्विसदनीय विधानमण्डल है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Mnemonic for the 6 bicameral states: KUMBAT (Karnataka, UP, Maharashtra, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana).
2. Under Article 171, the maximum strength of a Vidhan Parishad is 1/3rd of the Vidhan Sabha's strength, and the minimum is 40.
3. Under Article 169, Parliament can create or abolish a State Legislative Council on a special-majority resolution of that state's Vidhan Sabha.
qe:
Consider the following statements about Bicameral Legislatures:
Statement I: In a federal polity, the Upper House generally represents the constituent states or federal units.
Statement II: In India, all 28 states currently have bicameral legislatures with both a Vidhan Sabha and a Vidhan Parishad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
oe: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II

q:
सूची-I (राजनीतिक विचारक) को सूची-II (पुस्तक/अवधारणा) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I:
1. ए. वी. डायसी
2. लॉर्ड ब्राइस
3. हैरॉल्ड लास्की
4. हरमन फाइनर
सूची-II:
(a) ए ग्रामर ऑफ पॉलिटिक्स
(b) थ्योरी एंड प्रैक्टिस ऑफ मॉडर्न गवर्नमेंट
(c) इंट्रोडक्शन टू द स्टडी ऑफ द लॉ ऑफ द कॉन्स्टिट्यूशन
(d) मॉडर्न डेमोक्रेसीज
e:
A. V. Dicey authored 'Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution' (Rule of Law); Lord Bryce wrote 'Modern Democracies'; Harold Laski wrote 'A Grammar of Politics'; Herman Finer wrote 'Theory and Practice of Modern Government' (1-c, 2-d, 3-a, 4-b)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. A. V. Dicey is famous for elaborating the three pillars of 'Rule of Law' (विधि का शासन).
2. Lord Bryce famously said: "The best test of the excellence of a government is the efficiency of its judicial system."
3. James Madison wrote Federalist Paper No. 51 on Checks and Balances ("Ambition must be made to counteract ambition").
qe:
Match List-I (Political Thinker) with List-II (Book / Concept on Forms of Government) and select the correct code:
List-I:
1. A. V. Dicey
2. Lord Bryce
3. Harold Laski
4. Herman Finer
List-II:
(a) A Grammar of Politics
(b) Theory and Practice of Modern Government
(c) Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution
(d) Modern Democracies

q: भारतीय संविधान का कौन-सा अनुच्छेद चुनावों के अधीक्षण, निदेशन और नियंत्रण के लिए एक स्वतंत्र भारत निर्वाचन आयोग की स्थापना करता है?
e:
Article 324 (Part XV) establishes the Election Commission of India (अनुच्छेद 324 भारत निर्वाचन आयोग से संबंधित है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Article 325: No person to be ineligible for inclusion in electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste, or sex.
2. Article 326: Universal Adult Suffrage (वयस्क मताधिकार) for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections.
3. Article 329: Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters (delimitation and ongoing election process).
qe: Which Article of the Indian Constitution establishes an independent Election Commission of India to superintend, direct, and control elections?

q: किस संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम द्वारा भारत में न्यूनतम मतदान आयु को 21 वर्ष से घटाकर 18 वर्ष किया गया था?
e:
The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 (effective 28 March 1989) amended Article 326 to lower the voting age from 21 to 18 years (61वें संविधान संशोधन द्वारा मतदान आयु 21 से 18 वर्ष की गई)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. This reform was enacted during the Prime Ministership of Rajiv Gandhi, following recommendations of the Tarkunde Committee (1974–75).
2. India was among the earliest developing democracies to adopt Universal Adult Suffrage right from its first General Election (1951–52).
3. Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India; V. S. Ramadevi was the first woman CEC.
qe: By which Constitutional Amendment Act was the minimum voting age in India lowered from 21 years to 18 years?

q:
सूची-I (चुनाव सुधार समिति) को सूची-II (प्रमुख सिफारिश/विषय) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I:
1. तारकुंडे समिति (1974–75)
2. दिनेश गोस्वामी समिति (1990)
3. इंद्रजीत गुप्ता समिति (1998)
4. वोहरा समिति (1993)
सूची-II:
(a) अपराध और राजनीति के बीच सांठगांठ
(b) चुनावों का राज्य वित्तपोषण (State Funding)
(c) ईवीएम (EVM) एवं मतदाता फोटो पहचान पत्र
(d) मतदान आयु 18 वर्ष व बहुसदस्यीय निर्वाचन आयोग
e:
Tarkunde Committee (appointed by Jayaprakash Narayan) recommended voting age 18 & 3-member ECI; Dinesh Goswami Committee pushed EVMs & EPIC; Indrajit Gupta Committee recommended partial state funding of elections; Vohra Committee investigated the politician-criminal nexus (1-d, 2-c, 3-b, 4-a)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. The Election Commission became permanently multi-member (1 CEC + 2 ECs) in October 1993.
2. In 1982, EVMs were first used on a trial basis in Paravur Assembly constituency, Kerala; Goa (1999) was the first state to use EVMs in all constituencies.
3. The 2004 Lok Sabha election was the first General Election held completely with EVMs.
qe:
Match List-I (Electoral Reform Committee) with List-II (Key Recommendation / Focus) and select the correct code:
List-I:
1. Tarkunde Committee (1974–75)
2. Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990)
3. Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998)
4. Vohra Committee (1993)
List-II:
(a) Nexus between crime and politics
(b) State funding of elections
(c) EVMs and voter photo ID cards (EPIC)
(d) Lowering voting age to 18 & multi-member ECI

q: भारतीय संविधान की दसवीं अनुसूची में दल-बदल विरोधी कानून किस संविधान संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया था?
e:
The 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985 added the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) to curb political defections (52वें संशोधन 1985 द्वारा दसवीं अनुसूची जोड़ी गई)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. The 91st Amendment Act (2003) deleted the 'one-third split' exemption, retaining only the 'two-thirds merger' exemption, and capped Council of Ministers size at 15% of the lower house.
2. Questions of disqualification under the 10th Schedule are decided by the Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman) of the House.
3. In Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992), the Supreme Court held that the Speaker's decision under the 10th Schedule is subject to Judicial Review.
qe: The Anti-Defection Law (दल-बदल विरोधी कानून) was inserted into the Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution by which Constitutional Amendment?

q: भारतीय इलेक्ट्रॉनिक मतदान प्रणाली के संदर्भ में संक्षिप्त शब्द 'VVPAT' का पूर्ण रूप क्या है?
e:
VVPAT stands for 'Voter Verified Paper Audit Trail', allowing voters to visually verify for 7 seconds that their vote was cast for their intended candidate (VVPAT का पूर्ण रूप Voter Verified Paper Audit Trail है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. VVPAT was first used in a bye-election in Noksen Assembly constituency of Nagaland in September 2013.
2. The 2019 Lok Sabha election was the first General Election with 100% VVPAT coverage across all polling stations.
3. NOTA (None of the Above) was introduced in 2013 following the Supreme Court judgment in PUCL v. Union of India (2013).
qe: What does the acronym 'VVPAT' stand for in the context of Indian electronic voting systems?

q: भारत में लोकसभा और राज्य विधानसभाओं के चुनावों के लिए किस निर्वाचन प्रणाली का उपयोग किया जाता है?
e:
Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha elections use the First-Past-The-Post (FPTP) / Simple Plurality System in single-member territorial constituencies—whoever secures the highest number of votes wins (लोकसभा और विधानसभा चुनाव 'अग्रता ही विजेता' या FPTP प्रणाली से होते हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote (PR-STV) is used for elections to the President, Vice-President, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Councils.
2. Thomas Hare is credited with inventing the Single Transferable Vote (STV) system ('Hare System').
3. FPTP ensures clear legislative majorities and direct accountability to a constituency, though it can under-represent smaller parties.
qe: In India, which electoral system is used for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies?

q: भारतीय चुनावों में NOTA (इनमें से कोई नहीं) विकल्प के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही है?
o: If NOTA receives the highest number of votes in a Lok Sabha constituency, the election is automatically cancelled and re-polled.
NOTA is available in Rajya Sabha elections as well as Lok Sabha elections.
Even if NOTA secures the highest votes in a Lok Sabha election, the candidate with the next highest votes is declared elected.
NOTA was introduced by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act.
e:
Under current Indian law, NOTA does NOT have a 'right to reject'—if NOTA gets the most votes in a Lok Sabha/Assembly seat, the candidate securing the highest votes among contesting candidates is still declared elected (वर्तमान कानून में NOTA को सर्वाधिक मत मिलने पर भी सर्वाधिक मत पाने वाला प्रत्याशी ही विजयी घोषित होता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. In 2018, the Supreme Court disallowed NOTA in Rajya Sabha elections because Rajya Sabha uses open-ballot proportional representation, not direct secret ballot.
2. NOTA was introduced on EVM ballots in 2013 following the PUCL v. Union of India verdict.
3. The Election Commission of India's Model Code of Conduct (MCC) comes into force immediately upon announcement of election schedules (not statutory, enforced under Art. 324).
qe: Which of the following statements regarding the NOTA (None of the Above) option in Indian elections is correct?
oe: If NOTA receives the highest number of votes in a Lok Sabha constituency, the election is automatically cancelled and re-polled.
NOTA is available in Rajya Sabha elections as well as Lok Sabha elections.
Even if NOTA secures the highest votes in a Lok Sabha election, the candidate with the next highest votes is declared elected.
NOTA was introduced by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act.

q: दल-बदल के अतिरिक्त अन्य आधारों (जैसे अनुच्छेद 102 के तहत लाभ का पद धारण करना) पर किसी संसद सदस्य की अयोग्यता से संबंधित विवादों का निर्णय कौन करता है?
o: President of India, in accordance with the binding opinion of the Election Commission
Prime Minister in consultation with the Law Minister
e:
Under Article 103, the President decides disqualification matters (other than 10th Schedule defection) after obtaining the opinion of the Election Commission, and must act according to that opinion (अनुच्छेद 103 के तहत राष्ट्रपति निर्वाचन आयोग की राय के अनुसार निर्णय लेते हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Correspondingly, for State Legislators (Article 192), the Governor decides according to the Election Commission's opinion.
2. Disqualification on grounds of defection (10th Schedule) is decided by the Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman).
3. Election petitions challenging the validity of an MP/MLA's election are heard by the respective High Court under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
qe: Who decides disputes regarding the disqualification of a Member of Parliament on grounds OTHER than defection (such as holding an office of profit under Article 102)?
oe: President of India, in accordance with the binding opinion of the Election Commission
Prime Minister in consultation with the Law Minister

q: भारत के मुख्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त (CEC) का कार्यकाल कितना होता है?
o: 5 years or up to 62 years of age
6 years or up to 62 years of age
5 years or up to 65 years of age
6 years or up to 65 years of age
e:
The CEC and Election Commissioners hold office for a term of 6 years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier (6 वर्ष अथवा 65 वर्ष की आयु, जो भी पहले हो)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. The CEC enjoys security of tenure equivalent to a Supreme Court Judge; other Election Commissioners cannot be removed except on the recommendation of the CEC.
2. Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, they are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a 3-member Selection Committee (PM, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and a Union Cabinet Minister).
3. Their salaries and allowances are equivalent to those of a Supreme Court Judge.
qe: What is the tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India?
oe: 5 years or up to 62 years of age
6 years or up to 62 years of age
5 years or up to 65 years of age
6 years or up to 65 years of age

q: आनुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व की एकल संक्रमणीय मत (STV) प्रणाली (ड्रूप कोटा) में, यदि 3 रिक्त सीटों के लिए 1,000 वैध मत पड़े हों, तो एक प्रत्याशी के निर्वाचित होने के लिए न्यूनतम कितने मतों का कोटा आवश्यक होगा?
e:
Droop Quota = [Total Valid Votes ÷ (Number of Seats + 1)] + 1 = [1000 ÷ (3 + 1)] + 1 = 250 + 1 = 251 votes (ड्रूप कोटा = [कुल वैध मत ÷ (सीटें + 1)] + 1 = 251 मत)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. For a single-seat election (like the President of India), Quota = (Total Valid Votes ÷ 2) + 1 (i.e., >50% absolute majority).
2. Proportional Representation ensures minority opinions gain representation roughly proportional to their vote share.
3. J. S. Mill strongly advocated Proportional Representation in 'Considerations on Representative Government' (1861).
qe: In the Single Transferable Vote (STV) system of Proportional Representation (Droop Quota), if there are 1,000 valid votes cast for 3 vacant seats, what is the minimum quota of votes required for a candidate to be elected?

q: जनगणना के बाद संसदीय और विधानसभा निर्वाचन क्षेत्रों की क्षेत्रीय सीमाओं का पुनर्निर्धारण करने के लिए कौन-सा निकाय संवैधानिक रूप से अधिकृत है, जिसके आदेशों को किसी न्यायालय में चुनौती नहीं दी जा सकती?
e:
The Delimitation Commission (constituted by Parliament under Article 82) redraws constituency boundaries; under Article 329(a), its orders have the force of law and cannot be questioned in any court (परिसीमन आयोग के आदेशों को किसी न्यायालय में चुनौती नहीं दी जा सकती)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. India has constituted four Delimitation Commissions so far: 1952, 1963, 1973, and 2002 (chaired by Justice Kuldip Singh).
2. The 84th Constitutional Amendment Act (2001) froze the total number of Lok Sabha and Assembly seats per state based on the 1971 Census until the first Census taken after 2026.
3. The 87th Amendment (2003) allowed internal readjustment of constituencies based on the 2001 Census without altering total seats per state.
qe: Which body is constitutionally empowered to redraw the territorial boundaries of Parliamentary and Assembly constituencies after a Census, and whose orders cannot be challenged in any court?

q: भारतीय चुनावों में राजनीतिक वैज्ञानिकों द्वारा 'मतदान व्यवहार' के एक प्रमुख निर्धारक के रूप में निम्नलिखित में से किस कारक का व्यापक अध्ययन किया जाता है?
o: नेतृत्व का करिश्मा व दल की विचारधारा
e:
Indian voting behaviour is shaped by an interplay of socio-cultural factors (caste, religion, region, language) and rational/economic factors (incumbency performance, welfare delivery, leadership, and ideology) (भारतीय मतदान व्यवहार में उपर्युक्त सभी कारक महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाते हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Rajni Kothari famously analysed the 'politicization of caste' in Indian democracy in 'Caste in Indian Politics' (1970).
2. Yogendra Yadav and CSDS-Lokniti pioneered large-scale National Election Studies (NES) in India.
3. Increasing voter turnout among women and youth has been a notable trend in recent Indian elections.
qe: Which of the following factors is widely studied by political scientists as a major determinant of 'Voting Behaviour' (मतदान व्यवहार) in Indian elections?

q: जनप्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1951 (धारा 8(3)) और सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के लिली थॉमस बनाम भारत संघ (2013) निर्णय के अनुसार, किसी वर्तमान सांसद या विधायक को कितने वर्ष या अधिक के कारावास की सजा होने पर तत्काल अयोग्य घोषित कर दिया जाता है?
e:
Conviction with a sentence of 2 years or more triggers immediate disqualification under Section 8(3) of RPA 1951, plus a 6-year bar after release; Lily Thomas (2013) struck down Section 8(4) that previously gave sitting legislators a 3-month appeal buffer (2 वर्ष या अधिक की सजा पर तत्काल अयोग्यता लागू होती है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. RPA 1950 deals with allocation of seats, delimitation, and preparation of electoral rolls; RPA 1951 deals with conduct of elections, qualifications/disqualifications, and election disputes.
2. In Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR, 2002), the Supreme Court made disclosure of criminal antecedents, assets, liabilities, and educational qualifications mandatory for candidates.
3. In 2024, the Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bonds Scheme (2018) as unconstitutional for violating voters' Right to Information under Article 19(1)(a).
qe: Under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (Section 8(3)) and the Supreme Court's Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013) judgment, a sitting MP or MLA is immediately disqualified if convicted of an offence and sentenced to imprisonment for not less than:

q: भारत निर्वाचन आयोग द्वारा किसी राजनीतिक दल को 'राष्ट्रीय दल' के रूप में मान्यता प्राप्त करने के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी शर्त नहीं है?
o: Securing at least 6% of valid votes in 4 or more states in Lok Sabha/Assembly polls plus winning 4 Lok Sabha seats.
Winning at least 2% of total Lok Sabha seats (11 seats) from at least 3 different states.
Being recognized as a State Party in at least 4 states.
Securing at least 10% of valid votes in any 2 states in a Lok Sabha election.
e:
A party becomes a National Party if it meets ANY of the three conditions in A, B, or C; '10% votes in any 2 states' is NOT a valid criterion under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968 (किन्हीं 2 राज्यों में 10% मत की कोई शर्त नहीं है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Recognized National Parties get a reserved election symbol nationwide, free broadcast time on Doordarshan/AIR, and up to 40 star campaigners.
2. The Election Symbols Order, 1968 empowers ECI to recognize parties and resolve symbol disputes (e.g., Sadiq Ali case, 1971).
3. Registered unrecognized political parties do not get a permanently reserved symbol.
qe: Which of the following is NOT one of the criteria for a political party to be recognized as a 'National Party' by the Election Commission of India?
oe: Securing at least 6% of valid votes in 4 or more states in Lok Sabha/Assembly polls plus winning 4 Lok Sabha seats.
Winning at least 2% of total Lok Sabha seats (11 seats) from at least 3 different states.
Being recognized as a State Party in at least 4 states.
Securing at least 10% of valid votes in any 2 states in a Lok Sabha election.

q: 11 दिसंबर 1946 को भारत की संविधान सभा का स्थायी अध्यक्ष किसे चुना गया था?
e:
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946, succeeding interim President Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha (who presided over the first sitting on 9 December 1946) (डॉ. राजेन्द्र प्रसाद संविधान सभा के स्थायी अध्यक्ष थे)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. H. C. Mukherjee and V. T. Krishnamachari were Vice-Presidents; Sir B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor.
2. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was Chairman of the 7-member Drafting Committee (constituted 29 August 1947).
3. The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 (2 years, 11 months, 18 days) and came into full force on 26 January 1950.
qe: Who was elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly of India on 11 December 1946?

q: 42वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1976 द्वारा भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना में कौन-से तीन शब्द जोड़े गए थे?
e:
The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) amended the Preamble only once in Indian history, inserting 'Socialist' (समाजवादी), 'Secular' (पंथनिरपेक्ष), and 'Integrity' (अखंडता)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. The Preamble is based on the 'Objectives Resolution' moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946 and adopted on 22 January 1947.
2. In Berubari Union (1960), SC said Preamble is NOT part of the Constitution; in Kesavananda Bharati (1973), SC overruled it and held Preamble IS an integral part of the Constitution.
3. The ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity in the Preamble were inspired by the French Revolution (1789), and Social/Economic/Political Justice by the Russian Revolution (1917).
qe: Which three words were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?

q:
सूची-I (भारतीय संविधान का गृहीत प्रावधान) को सूची-II (स्रोत देश) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I:
1. राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व (DPSP)
2. मौलिक अधिकार व न्यायिक पुनरावलोकन
3. समवर्ती सूची व संयुक्त बैठक
4. आपातकाल में मौलिक अधिकारों का निलंबन
सूची-II:
(a) जर्मनी का वाइमर संविधान
(b) ऑस्ट्रेलिया
(c) संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका
(d) आयरलैंड
e:
DPSP was borrowed from Ireland, Fundamental Rights & Judicial Review from USA, Concurrent List & Joint Sitting from Australia, and suspension of FR during Emergency from Weimar Germany (1-d, 2-c, 3-b, 4-a)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Procedure for Constitutional Amendment (Art. 368) was borrowed from South Africa.
2. 'Procedure established by law' (Art. 21) was borrowed from Japan; 'Rule of Law' & Parliamentary system from the UK.
3. Over half the structural provisions of the Indian Constitution were drawn from the Government of India Act, 1935.
qe:
Match List-I (Borrowed Feature of Indian Constitution) with List-II (Source Country) and select the correct code:
List-I:
1. Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)
2. Fundamental Rights & Judicial Review
3. Concurrent List & Joint Sitting
4. Emergency Suspension of Fundamental Rights
List-II:
(a) Weimar Constitution of Germany
(b) Australia
(c) United States of America
(d) Ireland

q: डॉ. बी. आर. अम्बेडकर ने किस मौलिक अधिकार को 'संविधान का हृदय और आत्मा' कहा था?
o: Right to Life and Personal Liberty (Article 21)
e:
Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) the very 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' because without enforcement remedies, rights are meaningless (अनुच्छेद 32 को संविधान की आत्मा कहा गया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Under Article 32, the Supreme Court can issue 5 writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto.
2. High Courts issue writs under Article 226 (which has wider territorial/subject jurisdiction as it covers both FRs and ordinary legal rights).
3. Thakur Das Bhargava called the Preamble the 'Soul of the Constitution', while Granville Austin called FRs and DPSP together the 'Conscience of the Constitution'.
qe: Which Fundamental Right was famously described by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution'?
oe: Right to Life and Personal Liberty (Article 21)

q: 44वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1978 द्वारा किस मौलिक अधिकार को भाग III से हटाकर अनुच्छेद 300A के अंतर्गत विधिक अधिकार बना दिया गया?
e:
The 44th Amendment (1978, Morarji Desai government) repealed Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31, shifting Right to Property to Article 300A (Part XII) as a constitutional legal right (44वें संशोधन द्वारा सम्पत्ति के अधिकार को मौलिक अधिकार से हटाकर विधिक अधिकार बनाया गया)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Originally there were 7 Fundamental Rights; after the 44th Amendment, there are 6 categories of Fundamental Rights.
2. Articles 20 and 21 can NEVER be suspended even during a National Emergency (44th Amendment).
3. Right to Privacy was unanimously declared a Fundamental Right under Article 21 in K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017, 9-judge bench).
qe: Which Fundamental Right was removed from Part III by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 and made a legal right under Article 300A?

q: भारतीय संविधान के भाग III के अंतर्गत मौलिक अधिकारों का कौन-सा समूह केवल भारतीय नागरिकों को प्राप्त है, विदेशियों को नहीं?
e:
Five Fundamental Rights—Articles 15, 16, 19, 29, and 30—are available EXCLUSIVELY to Indian citizens (अनुच्छेद 15, 16, 19, 29 और 30 केवल भारतीय नागरिकों को प्राप्त हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Articles 14, 20, 21, 21A, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, and 28 are available to both citizens and foreigners (except enemy aliens for Art. 22).
2. Article 17 abolishes Untouchability (absolute right, enforceable against private individuals too).
3. Article 18 abolishes Titles (except military and academic distinctions; Bharat Ratna/Padma awards are national honours, not titles — Balaji Raghavan case, 1996).
qe: Which set of Fundamental Rights under Part III of the Indian Constitution is available ONLY to Indian citizens and NOT to foreigners (aliens)?

q: सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के किस ऐतिहासिक निर्णय (13-न्यायाधीशों की पीठ, 7:6 बहुमत) में 'मूल ढाँचा सिद्धांत' (Basic Structure Doctrine) प्रतिपादित किया गया?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
e:
On 24 April 1973, in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, the Supreme Court held that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution under Article 368, including Fundamental Rights, PROVIDED it does not alter the 'Basic Structure' (केशवानन्द भारती वाद 1973 में मूल ढाँचा सिद्धांत प्रतिपादित हुआ)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Golaknath (1967) had held Parliament could not amend FRs at all; Kesavananda overruled Golaknath while introducing Basic Structure limits.
2. Minerva Mills (1980) held that harmony and balance between FRs and DPSP is itself part of the Basic Structure.
3. Maneka Gandhi (1978) expanded Article 21 by reading 'Due Process of Law' (fair, just, and reasonable procedure) into 'Procedure established by law'.
qe: In which landmark Supreme Court judgment (13-judge bench, 7:6 majority) was the 'Basic Structure Doctrine' (मूल ढाँचा सिद्धांत) propounded?
oe: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)

q:
सूची-I (मौलिक अधिकार अनुच्छेद) को सूची-II (प्रावधान) से सुमेलित कीजिए तथा सही कूट चुनिए:
सूची-I:
1. अनुच्छेद 17
2. अनुच्छेद 23
3. अनुच्छेद 24
4. अनुच्छेद 25
सूची-II:
(a) अंतःकरण और धर्म की स्वतंत्रता
(b) कारखानों में बाल श्रम का निषेध
(c) मानव दुर्व्यापार एवं बलात् श्रम का निषेध
(d) अस्पृश्यता का अंत
e:
Art. 17 abolishes Untouchability; Art. 23 prohibits human trafficking & begar (forced labour); Art. 24 prohibits child labour (<14 years) in hazardous factories/mines; Art. 25 guarantees freedom of conscience & religion (1-d, 2-c, 3-b, 4-a)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Articles 23 and 24 constitute the 'Right against Exploitation' (शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार).
2. Articles 25–28 constitute the 'Right to Freedom of Religion'; Articles 29–30 constitute 'Cultural and Educational Rights'.
3. The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 gives statutory teeth to Article 17.
qe:
Match List-I (Fundamental Right Article) with List-II (Provision) and select the correct code:
List-I:
1. Article 17
2. Article 23
3. Article 24
4. Article 25
List-II:
(a) Freedom of conscience and religion
(b) Prohibition of employment of children in factories
(c) Prohibition of human trafficking and forced labour
(d) Abolition of Untouchability

q: राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व (DPSP) भारतीय संविधान के किस भाग और किन अनुच्छेदों में निहित हैं?
e:
DPSP are contained in Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) and are non-justiciable (Article 37), though fundamental in the governance of the country (भाग IV, अनुच्छेद 36 से 51 में नीति निदेशक तत्व हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described DPSP as a 'Novel Feature' of the Indian Constitution, aiming to establish 'Economic and Social Democracy' (Welfare State).
2. K. T. Shah famously criticized DPSP as 'a cheque payable at the convenience of the bank'.
3. Fundamental Rights establish Political Democracy, while DPSP establish Social and Economic Democracy.
qe: Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are enshrined in which Part and Articles of the Constitution of India?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा नीति निदेशक तत्व 'गांधीवादी सिद्धांत' को प्रतिबिंबित करता है?
o: Promotion of International Peace and Security (Article 51)
e:
Article 40 (Organization of Village Panchayats) is a quintessential Gandhian DPSP; Articles 44, 50, and 51 are Liberal-Intellectual principles (अनुच्छेद 40 ग्राम पंचायतों का गठन गांधीवादी सिद्धांत है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Other Gandhian DPSPs: Art. 43 (cottage industries), Art. 43B (cooperative societies — 97th Amendment), Art. 46 (SC/ST/weaker sections), Art. 47 (prohibition of intoxicating drinks), Art. 48 (cow slaughter ban).
2. Socialist DPSPs: Arts. 38, 39, 39A (free legal aid), 41, 42, 43, 43A (workers' participation in management), 47.
3. Liberal-Intellectual DPSPs: Arts. 44 (UCC), 45 (early childhood care), 48 (modern agriculture), 48A (environment — 42nd Amendment), 49 (monuments), 50, 51.
qe: Which of the following Directive Principles of State Policy reflects a 'Gandhian Principle' (गांधीवादी सिद्धांत)?
oe: Promotion of International Peace and Security (Article 51)

q: भारतीय संविधान का कौन-सा अनुच्छेद राज्य को भारत के समस्त राज्यक्षेत्र में नागरिकों के लिए एक 'समान नागरिक संहिता' (Uniform Civil Code) सुनिश्चित करने का प्रयास करने का निर्देश देता है?
e:
Article 44 (Liberal-Intellectual DPSP) directs the State to endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code throughout India (अनुच्छेद 44 समान नागरिक संहिता से संबंधित है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Goa has followed a common civil code (Portuguese Civil Code of 1867) since before liberation; Uttarakhand became the first Indian state post-independence to enact a Uniform Civil Code Act (2024).
2. Article 42 provides for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
3. Article 48A (added by 42nd Amendment, 1976) directs protection and improvement of environment, forests, and wildlife.
qe: Which Article of the Constitution of India directs the State to endeavour to secure a 'Uniform Civil Code' (समान नागरिक संहिता) for citizens throughout the territory of India?

q: 42वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1976 द्वारा संविधान के भाग IV में कौन-से नीति निदेशक तत्व नए जोड़े गए थे?
e:
The 42nd Amendment (1976) added four DPSP provisions: Art. 39(f) (healthy development of children), Art. 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Art. 43A (participation of workers in management of industries), and Art. 48A (protection of environment & wildlife) (42वें संशोधन द्वारा अनुच्छेद 39A, 43A, 48A जोड़े गए)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. 44th Amendment (1978) added Art. 38(2) (minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities).
2. 86th Amendment (2002) modified Art. 45 (early childhood care & education below age 6).
3. 97th Amendment (2011) added Art. 43B (promotion of cooperative societies).
qe: Which Directive Principles were newly added to Part IV of the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?

q:
मौलिक अधिकारों (FR) और नीति निदेशक तत्वों (DPSP) के टकराव के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: चम्पकम दोराईराजन (1951) वाद में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने कहा कि टकराव की स्थिति में मौलिक अधिकार DPSP पर अभिभावी (प्रभावी) होंगे।
कथन II: मिनर्वा मिल्स (1980) वाद में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने निर्णय दिया कि संविधान मौलिक अधिकारों और DPSP के संतुलन की नींव पर आधारित है।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II
e:
Both statements accurately trace the landmark constitutional evolution of FR vs DPSP jurisprudence (दोनों कथन पूर्णतः सत्य हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Currently, only DPSPs under Article 39(b) and 39(c) enjoy immunity against challenges under Articles 14 and 19 (via Article 31C, upheld in Kesavananda Bharati).
2. The 42nd Amendment tried to extend Art. 31C immunity to ALL DPSPs, which the Supreme Court struck down in Minerva Mills (1980).
3. Champakam Dorairajan (1951) led directly to the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951 (inserting Article 15(4) for reservations).
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding the conflict between Fundamental Rights (FR) and Directive Principles (DPSP):
Statement I: In Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Supreme Court held that in case of conflict, Fundamental Rights prevail over DPSP.
Statement II: In Minerva Mills (1980), the Supreme Court ruled that the Constitution is founded on the bedrock of balance between FRs and DPSP, and neither has absolute primacy over the other.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
oe: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II

q: किस संवैधानिक रिट का शाब्दिक अर्थ 'सशरीर प्रस्तुत करना' होता है और जो अवैध निरोध के विरुद्ध व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का रक्षक है?
e:
Habeas Corpus ('to have the body of') commands the detaining authority (public or private) to produce the detained person before the court to verify legality of detention (बंदी प्रत्यक्षीकरण अवैध हिरासत के विरुद्ध व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का सबसे प्रभावी कवच है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Habeas Corpus is the ONLY writ that can be issued against both public authorities AND private individuals.
2. Mandamus cannot be issued against a private individual, the President, or State Governors.
3. Prohibition is preventive (issued while proceedings are pending), whereas Certiorari is both preventive and curative (quashes an order already passed).
qe: Which Constitutional Writ literally means 'To have the body of' and serves as a bulwark of individual liberty against illegal detention?

q: भारतीय संविधान का कौन-सा अनुच्छेद भाग III (मौलिक अधिकार) और भाग IV (नीति निदेशक तत्व) के प्रयोजनों के लिए 'राज्य' (State) शब्द को परिभाषित करता है?
e:
Article 12 defines 'State' to include the Government & Parliament of India, State Governments & Legislatures, all local authorities (Panchayats, Municipalities), and other statutory/non-statutory authorities like LIC, ONGC, SAIL (अनुच्छेद 12 'राज्य' को परिभाषित करता है; अनुच्छेद 36 इसे भाग IV पर लागू करता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Article 13 declares all laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights to be void (basis of Judicial Review).
2. Doctrines linked to Article 13: Doctrine of Eclipse (आच्छादन का सिद्धांत), Doctrine of Severability (पृथक्करणीयता का सिद्धांत), and Doctrine of Waiver.
3. Article 14 contains two expressions: 'Equality before law' (British origin, negative concept) and 'Equal protection of laws' (US origin, positive concept).
qe: Which Article of the Constitution of India defines the term 'State' (राज्य) for the purposes of Part III (Fundamental Rights) and Part IV (DPSP)?

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 19(1) के अंतर्गत वर्तमान में भारतीय नागरिकों को कितनी स्वतंत्रताएँ प्रत्याभूत हैं?
e:
Originally Article 19(1) guaranteed 7 freedoms; after deletion of 19(1)(f) (Right to Property) by the 44th Amendment (1978), 6 freedoms remain: speech & expression, peaceful assembly, associations/unions/cooperatives, free movement, residence, and profession/trade (वर्तमान में अनुच्छेद 19(1) में 6 स्वतंत्रताएँ हैं)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Freedom of the Press is implicitly included in Article 19(1)(a) (Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras, 1950).
2. Cooperative societies were added to Article 19(1)(c) by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011.
3. Reasonable restrictions on Article 19(1)(a) are specified in Article 19(2).
qe: How many freedoms are currently guaranteed to Indian citizens under Article 19(1) of the Constitution of India?

q: भारतीय संविधान का कौन-सा अनुच्छेद भूतलक्षी दांडिक विधियों, दोहरे दंड (double jeopardy) और आत्म-अभिशंसन (self-incrimination) से संरक्षण प्रदान करता है?
e:
Article 20 grants three vital criminal-law safeguards: Art. 20(1) No ex-post facto law; Art. 20(2) No double jeopardy; Art. 20(3) No self-incrimination (अनुच्छेद 20 अपराधों के लिए दोषसिद्धि के संबंध में संरक्षण देता है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Article 22 provides protection against arbitrary arrest and detention (right to be informed of grounds, right to consult a lawyer, production before a magistrate within 24 hours).
2. Article 20(1) applies only to criminal laws, NOT to civil or tax laws.
3. Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during an Emergency under Article 359.
qe: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees protection against ex-post facto criminal laws, double jeopardy, and self-incrimination?

q: भारत की संविधान सभा में 'संघ संविधान समिति' और 'संघ शक्ति समिति' के अध्यक्ष कौन थे?
e:
Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the Union Powers Committee, Union Constitution Committee, and States Committee (जवाहरलाल नेहरू संघ संविधान समिति व संघ शक्ति समिति के अध्यक्ष थे)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee and Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities & Tribal Areas.
2. J. B. Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee; H. C. Mukherjee chaired the Minorities Sub-Committee.
3. Dr. Rajendra Prasad chaired the Rules of Procedure Committee and Steering Committee.
qe: Who was the Chairman of the 'Union Constitution Committee' and the 'Union Powers Committee' in the Constituent Assembly of India?

q: भारतीय संविधान की प्रमुख विशेषताओं के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
o: It is the lengthiest written constitution in the world.
It represents a blend of rigidity and flexibility in its amendment procedure.
It provides for an independent judiciary with a dual system of separate federal and state courts like the USA.
It establishes a secular state with no official state religion.
e:
Unlike the USA (which has dual courts — separate federal and state judiciaries), India has a SINGLE INTEGRATED judiciary with the Supreme Court at the apex, High Courts below it, and subordinate courts beneath them (भारत में अमेरिका की भाँति दोहरी न्यायपालिका नहीं बल्कि एकीकृत न्यायपालिका है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Originally the Constitution (1949) had a Preamble, 395 Articles (in 22 Parts), and 8 Schedules; today it has 12 Schedules and 25 Parts (still numbered up to 395 with lettered insertions).
2. Article 368 provides two formal amendment methods (special majority, and special majority + half-state ratification), while some provisions can be amended by simple majority outside Art. 368.
3. Sir Ivor Jennings famously called the Indian Constitution a 'Lawyer's Paradise'.
qe: Which of the following statements regarding the Salient Features of the Indian Constitution is NOT correct?
oe: It is the lengthiest written constitution in the world.
It represents a blend of rigidity and flexibility in its amendment procedure.
It provides for an independent judiciary with a dual system of separate federal and state courts like the USA.
It establishes a secular state with no official state religion.

q: भारतीय संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत राज्य को अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति और सुरक्षा की अभिवृद्धि, राष्ट्रों के बीच न्यायसंगत संबंध बनाए रखने और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय विवादों को मध्यस्थता से निपटाने का निर्देश दिया गया है?
e:
Article 51 (the final Article of Part IV — DPSP) lays down the constitutional foundation of India's foreign policy: promoting international peace, respect for international law & treaty obligations, and peaceful arbitration of disputes (अनुच्छेद 51 भारत की विदेश नीति व अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति से संबंधित है)।
Exam Booster Facts:
1. Article 49 directs protection of monuments, places, and objects of national importance.
2. Article 50 directs separation of judiciary from the executive in public services.
3. India's Panchsheel principles (1954) and Non-Alignment policy reflect the spirit of Article 51.
qe: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the State directed to promote international peace and security, maintain just and honourable relations between nations, and encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration?
